key_insight: Large pan-cancer foundation models outperformed an endometrial-cancer-specific feature extractor across morphology, molecular, and prognostic tasks, with no single model best for everything.
clinical_relevance: This suggests general-purpose pathology foundation models may be more useful than disease-specific features for supporting digital pathology research in endometrial cancer.
method: Evaluated 7 state-of-the-art foundation models on digitized endometrial cancer slides.
Compared performance on morphological, molecular, and prognostic prediction tasks.
Benchmarked against EsVIT, a model trained exclusively on endometrial cancer.
evidence_signal: The study used a large dataset of 3,293 patients from randomized trials and clinical cohorts, providing broad evaluation across multiple clinical tasks.
watch_item: Model selection remains difficult because performance differences were small in some areas and training-data details for the foundation models were limited.
paper_title: Assessing Foundation Models for Computational Pathology in Endometrial Cancer
